item.title: Jerry Seinfeld turns tables on radical anti-Israel agitators after chaotic Chicago stunt backfires
item.description: Viral video shows Jerry Seinfeld dancing and mocking anti-Israel hecklers at the Chicago Theatre as security escorted protesters from the venue.
item.content:encoded:
Comedian Jerry Seinfeld turned the tables on anti-Israel hecklers who attempted to derail his Chicago performance last Friday, mocking the protesters as security removed them from the venue.

Viral video from the confrontation shows activists shouting at Seinfeld at the Chicago Theatre, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" in Gaza and alleging that American taxpayer dollars are funding the deaths of thousands of civilians.

"Twenty-two thousand Palestinians who are children now are killed with our taxpayer money, and you’re making jokes!" a woman shouted in clips posted online.

JERRY SEINFELD GIVES BLUNT THREE-WORD RESPONSE TO INFLUENCER ASKING FOR A 'FREE PALESTINE'

Seinfeld then dances on stage and mocks the protesters with sarcastic remarks, calling himself "racist" and saying, "It’s a genocide. I’m into it." He also joked that he would find out how much the protesters paid for their tickets and send the money directly to Israel.

As security personnel escorted the demonstrators out of the auditorium, one audience member shouted, "Rough her up!"

The Anti-War Committee Chicago and the Chicago branch of the US Palestinian Community Network have taken credit for organizing the disruption, writing on Instagram, "Friday’s disruption sent a clear message: Those who defend Israel’s genocide and ethnic cleansing of Palestinians in Gaza and throughout Palestine will be met with protest and are not welcome on Chicago’s stages without opposition."

COMEDIAN DECLARES JERRY SEINFELD 'UNCANCELLABLE' DESPITE 'WOKE' ANTI-ISRAEL FESTIVAL BOYCOTT

Fox News Digital reached out to Seinfeld’s team for comment but did not hear back.

The altercation is the latest in a string of protests targeting the 72-year-old Jewish comedian over his staunch defense of Israel.

ANTI-ISRAEL PROTESTERS LABEL MAMDANI A 'TRAITOR,' ACCUSE HIM OF 'GENOCIDE' OUTSIDE OCT 7 VIGIL

Comedian and media analyst Tim Young told Fox News Digital he believes protesters are paying top dollar to hijack comedy shows for viral attention rather than political discourse.

"They know that once they start yelling, everyone will whip their cameras out, and it is a very direct interaction and maybe one of the only direct interactions protesters get to have with celebrities and with the internet," Young said.

"If you are in a very intimate environment where everyone is quiet, listening to one person, you will be heard. And, so, that's what they're taking advantage of here."

Young compared the disruptions at Seinfeld's shows to protests at political rallies, arguing that some activists are willing to pay steep ticket prices to confront the comedian.

"It seems like people are going to Jerry Seinfeld's shows like they're going to a Trump rally to protest," Young said. "They wanted to get Jerry's attention. They want to, for some reason, they're very, very adamant on getting him to react to the Israel-Palestine conflict."

Young also linked the disruptions to Seinfeld's past criticism of performing at universities.

30% OF COLLEGE STUDENTS SAY VIOLENCE ACCEPTABLE WAY TO STOP SPEAKERS ON CAMPUSES, SURVEY FINDS

"It's why Jerry doesn't like to go and perform at college campuses. And he said he hates performing at college campuses specifically for that reason," Young said. 

"He doesn't want to get into the political thing. He doesn't want to have protesters yelling back and forth with him. It's a waste of the rest of the audience's time, and he knows that."

In May 2024, dozens of students walked out during Seinfeld's commencement address at Duke University, some holding Palestinian flags. 

Seinfeld returned to the university in September 2025 to introduce freed Israeli hostage Omer Shem Tov at a campus event, where he addressed anti-Israel protests, saying, "Free Palestine is, to me, just — you’re free to say you don’t like Jews. Just say you don’t like Jews."

QUIET PART OUT LOUD: ANTI-ISRAEL MOBS WANT ONE STATE CALLED 'PALESTINE,' ERASING ISRAEL

"By saying ‘Free Palestine,’ you’re not admitting what you really think," he said. "So, it’s actually — compared to the Ku Klux Klan, I’m actually thinking the Klan is actually a little better here because they can come right out and say, ‘We don’t like Blacks, we don’t like Jews.’ OK, that’s honest."

Seinfeld also faced controversy overseas last month when several European acts withdrew from the inaugural MEO Commedia a La Carte Fest in Lisbon, Portugal, where he is scheduled to headline later this year.

The acts did not name Seinfeld directly in their withdrawal statements, but some cited concerns about the Israel-Gaza conflict. One performer said someone involved in the festival defended ideas they considered indefensible.

Young, who previously dismissed efforts to cancel Seinfeld over his support for Israel, argued that protesters target the billionaire comedian because of his influence and celebrity status.

"This is all about control. It's all about power. And it's all about the left having power over these very influential and powerful people," Young said. "And they’re not having it."

item.title: James McAvoy says ‘Band of Brothers’ co-star recruited fellow actors to bully him on set
item.description: James McAvoy revealed he was bullied on his first day filming "Band of Brothers" and named the co-stars who helped him through the experience.
item.content:encoded:
James McAvoy is getting candid about what it was like filming "Band of Brothers" and why it wasn't his best experience on a set.

During a recent appearance on "Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen," the actor was asked to rate his experience working on different projects, and when he was shown a picture of the show's cast, he said he was bullied during filming.

"On my first day on set, there was a ton of actors," he began. "It was one of those scenes with everybody in it, and we’re all at a bar, and I had a scene. And all these guys were in it for nine months, 10 months, and they get one line in one episode, and one line 10 episodes later. They were all pissed. I come in for one episode, and I’ve got an arc and scenes. I’ve got tons of lines."

When the photo, which featured many of his co-stars from the show, flashed on the screen, McAvoy got up to get a closer look, confirming that a specific actor was in the photo.

DEBI MAZAR SAYS 'ENTOURAGE' SET 'GOT TOXIC' AFTER SHE RETURNED FROM HAVING HER SECOND DAUGHTER

"So, one of the guys in that picture decided to bully me on my first day as a professional actor out of acting school," he said. "He got him and his buddies to just stand pointing at me and laugh at me for like three minutes."

While he didn't name names, the photo featured Donnie Wahlberg, Kirk Acevedo, Scott Grimes, Neal McDonough, Adam James, Frank John Hughes, Philip Barantini and Ross McCall.

The "X-Men: First Class" star added that not everyone on set participated in the bullying, saying Dexter Fletcher and Robin Laing "took me aside, and they were like, ‘Come hang with us, man.'"

He went on to say that he would give the overall experience on the show a nine out of 10 but noted "that day felt like a two."

"Band of Brothers" is a 10-part miniseries that aired on HBO in 2001 and told the story of Easy Company, 506th Regiment of the 101st Airborne Division, U.S. Army. The show's storylines were based on interviews with real-life survivors of Easy Company, in addition to letters and journals of real soldiers.

After his one episode on the show, McAvoy shot to stardom with roles in "The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe," "Wanted," "Atonement" and in the "X-Men" franchise.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

When speaking about how he got the role in "X-Men," McAvoy admitted to the "Happy Sad Confused" podcast in September 2024 that when he was first approached about starring in the project, he and his wife had taken some time off after the birth of their first child.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

While he said they "weren't penniless" and weren't in debt, he admitted they "had pretty much nothing in the bank," and he needed to get back to work. His main priority was staying close to home to still be there for his son, which, combined with the script, was a big upside when he heard about "X-Men: First Class."

"There's only like 60 pages of it at this point, and I feel like it's good Jane Goldman did a great job," he said of the script. 

"It's good, but it's incomplete. Don't really know where it's going. But I was like, 'This is a three-picture deal. They're paying well. It's 40 minutes from my front door. I'm a fan of the original material. I get to be young Charles Xavier.' And I was like, ‘This is a no-brainer.’

"So, my agent phoned me, and she was like, 'What do you think?' and I was like, 'It's a work of genius. We're doing it.'"

item.title: Obama's star power gets a reality check from Black voters in crucial Senate race: 'It's a turnoff'
item.description: Barack Obama's endorsement of Abdul El-Sayed drew mixed reactions from Black Detroit voters, with undecided residents saying it didn't move the needle.
item.content:encoded:
DETROIT — Former President Barack Obama’s endorsement of Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is getting a mixed reception among Black voters in Detroit, with some undecided voters saying the former president's backing isn't enough to win them over.

Fox News Digital spoke with more than a dozen Black voters in Detroit, most of whom said they plan to back El-Sayed in November, but several undecided voters said Obama's endorsement had not persuaded them to support the Democrat. The reactions come as Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers seeks to win over disaffected Democrats, including Black voters in Detroit, a key constituency for the party in Michigan.

"Honestly, it's a turn-off just because I've seen too many candidates use him just to manipulate the Democratic vote," Mercedes, one undecided Black voter, told Fox News Digital of Obama's endorsement.

BLACK VOTERS RIP DEMS OVER TAKING THEM FOR GRANTED IN EL-SAYED'S BACKYARD: ‘HUSH US UP’

"No, not at all," Anthony, another undecided Black voter, told Fox News Digital when asked if Obama’s endorsement had swayed him toward El-Sayed. "What he's been able to do is from an image standpoint, as far as ‘hope,’ he drove the point there. But as far as really giving back to the community, minority owned businesses, and everyone across the board, I don't really think he really got there for me … he really hasn't swayed me one way or another."

Obama and El-Sayed are preparing to campaign together in Michigan despite the Democratic Senate nominee's history of sharply criticizing the former president, a political reversal that also drew mixed reactions from Black Detroit voters interviewed by Fox News Digital.

Juanita, another Black voter who has yet to commit to El-Sayed, told Fox News Digital that, "I don't want to be pushed to vote for him because somebody else is backing him."

Rita, a Black voter who said she had recently been homeless, told Fox News Digital that she would prefer to do her own research rather than relying on Obama’s endorsement.

MICHIGAN SENATE CANDIDATE ABDUL EL-SAYED SAYS LEADERS MUST ADDRESS ‘UNPAID DEBTS’ TO BLACK COMMUNITIES

Even some voters who support El-Sayed stated that Obama’s endorsement didn’t do much for them.

"I think that a lot of people put more stock into who the person is than what he does … his yay or nay doesn't sway me either way," one such voter told Fox News Digital.

Detroit’s African American residents were not uniform in dismissing Obama’s endorsement, however. Roughly half of those who spoke with Fox News Digital said the former president’s backing improved their opinion of El-Sayed, though none of those voters claimed that they were undecided before the endorsement.

"For sure, I’m an Obama stan," Jamel, a Black voter planning to support El-Sayed, told Fox News Digital when asked whether Obama’s endorsement made him more likely to back the Democrat.

"Somebody who is endorsed by Obama, I would want to vote for them, because I stand behind the things he endorsed at the time, and I think that Obama’s endorsement means a lot to our community," Kenya, another Black voter, told Fox News Digital.

Detroit's Black voters were also divided over El-Sayed’s past criticism of Obama, particularly now that the two are preparing to campaign together.

‘DESTROYING THE AMERICAN WAY OF LIFE’: EL-SAYED’S POLITICAL ORBIT COMPLICATES EFFORT TO MODERATE HIS IMAGE

In a 2012 opinion column, El-Sayed accused then-President Obama of perpetuating war, violating civil liberties and deporting more people than any previous president. He described Obama’s reelection as "no victory," writing, "it was the rock we chose over the hard place."

El-Sayed has since walked back those criticisms, praising Obama’s handling of the circumstances he inherited and noting that it is possible to disagree with someone while still admiring them.

"Yeah, I don't understand how you can endorse somebody that was kind of the opposition when you were in office," Juanita told Fox News Digital. "I mean, that doesn't make sense."

"I think I see it as a flip flop, but I also see it as an opportunity to pretty much highlight those things and how he's actually changed and why their objectives may align now," Anthony said. "You know, people's objectives change, their perspectives change."

Nia, an African American voter who said she intends to support El-Sayed, said that pivots like El-Sayed’s are common in politics, pointing to Vice President JD Vance’s past criticism of President Donald Trump as an example.

Despite mixed reactions to Obama's endorsement and El-Sayed's past criticism, several Black voters interviewed by Fox News Digital acknowledged the former president's continuing influence within the Democratic Party.

HARRIS JOINS FORCES WITH RADICAL SENATE NOMINEE IN KEY SWING STATE AS 2028 WHISPERS SWIRL

"He is. I mean, you can't deny that he has a gigantic following and a lot of people will follow him and will listen to what he has to say," Vincent, a Black voter who voted early for El-Sayed, told Fox News Digital. "But we're coming into a point in time now where we want to see results on both sides. We're not seeing results from either party, so we have to see results. So he may still have a big sway in the party now, but I think party politics is coming to an end kind of quick."

While Fox News Digital's interviews were limited in number, they echo concerns about El-Sayed's support among Black voters that have surfaced in other reporting and polling. Pre-primary polling showed stronger support for Rep. Haley Stevens among Black Democratic voters, and questions have persisted about whether El-Sayed can consolidate that support heading into November.

A recent focus group of Black voters held by MS NOW, for instance, found reluctance among Black Michigan voters to cast their lot with El-Sayed. A Fox News poll conducted in late September found that just 77% of African American voters were supportive of El-Sayed, significantly below the usual Democratic benchmark for the demographic.

"I think he’s taking advantage [of] we as Black people are Democratic, and he think we gonna vote for him anyway," one middle-aged Black woman told the MS NOW panel. "And I’m like, ‘No sir, I’m gonna put uncommitted down on that little circle and move on.’ If you’re going to Congress to represent me, I need you to talk about what’s going on in this community."

While the GOP sees an opportunity here, the party has long attempted to court minority support, with mixed results.

Kandia Milton, a government affairs professional with deep ties to Detroit's African American community, pushed back against the narrative that El-Sayed would struggle with Black voters in November.

MICHIGAN DEMOCRAT HALEY STEVENS BACKS EL-SAYED AFTER NARROW PRIMARY DEFEAT, CALLS SOCIALISM ‘DANGEROUS’

"The great thing about Abdul is that he's not new to Detroiters. … And so Detroiters, once they understand his background, understand what he stands for and all the things that he's done in the past, you see greater enthusiasm for his campaign and his candidacy for Senate," Milton said of El-Sayed. 

"He has been very active in getting out into the community. In fact, tomorrow we have a public meeting with Abdul at our church. Where he will be speaking to the community around, you know, the issues that he stands on and stands firm on."

Milton characterized Obama's endorsement of El-Sayed as a "great shot in the arm" for his campaign, citing the former president's "credibility in our community" and arguing that the endorsement "puts to rest this notion that there's some tension between him and former President Obama." Milton wasn't surprised, however, that some Black voters said Obama's endorsement alone wasn't enough to win their support.

"I think so often we take for granted the fact that many of the voters are informed voters, all of them are informed voters, and so it's not just the fact that Obama supported him, thus I'm going to vote for Abdul. A lot of folks are doing their own research," Milton told Fox News Digital. "They're very curious about Abdul. They see a lot of him on social media, in the media, national media as well. And so it has raised eyebrows and a lot of curiosity around who this guy is."

Obama’s endorsement comes as both sides are trying to eke out every possible advantage they can in what is likely to be a very tight race. 

Fox News’ most recent Power Rankings has Michigan’s Senate race categorized as a "toss-up," meaning that neither party has an edge.

A representative for Obama and the El-Sayed campaign did not respond to requests for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Friday.

item.title: Brittany Mahomes stuns fans with her gym picture, Fitzy obliterates Bo Nix & is college football going to die?
item.description: Thursday Night Football saw Bo Nix rank dead last among 701 quarterbacks in average pass length as Ryan Fitzpatrick delivered a brutal takedown.
item.content:encoded:
Happy Friday — have we all cleansed ourselves of that Thursday Night Football game last night?

Goodness gracious. I thought I was immune to bad quarterback play given I've been a Dolphins fan for 25 years, but even I was disgusted by what I saw.

Sure, l may be a little biased because I had RJ Harvey at OVER 3.5 receptions and Bo Nix couldn't get him the ball in the second half if his life depended on it, but still ...

It was bad. It was gross. Wait till you see what Ryan Fitzpatrick had to say about it. Lordy.

Before that, though ... welcome to a Friday Nightcaps — the one where Brittany Mahomes hits the gym and shows America she still very much has the fastball.

What else? I've got college football continuing down its dangerous path with a 24-team playoff, the aforementioned Fitzpatrick takedown, and I don't do much soccer, but you HAVE to see this penalty kick from earlier in the week.

I have no idea who this cat is, where this game was played, or who these teams are ... but I'm all in. I can't stop watching. It's mesmerizing.

You'll see.

OK, grab you a Sears Christmas catalog and start circling things to celebrate National Department Store Day, and settle in for a Friday 'Cap!

Man, do I miss department stores. They were the best. Sure, some still kinda-sorta exist — I still have a Dillard's in my town, somehow — but it's not the same.

And today's youth will never, ever know the feeling. What a pleasure.

Sears, Macy's, JCPenney, Dillard's — all absolute staples in a shopping mall back in the '80s and '90s. They'd be in the four separate corners of the mall, and it was just a choose-your-own-adventure book every time you pulled into the parking lot.

Which entrance do we wanna choose? Do we feel like going through the Macy's perfume section to get to the Auntie Anne's in the food court because it's a quicker route? Is it gonna be weird when we have to walk by the Victoria's Secret with our parents? What are the chances we can convince them to give us some quarters for the arcade?

Wait, are those teriyaki chicken bites on a toothpick in the food court free?!

Man, we had it all. It was perfect. And for those who want just a little taste, here's a throwback to what I still consider the greatest commercial of all time, even all these years later:

Core memory unlocked. Chills, every time. That thing used to play 27 times an hour back in the day. It didn't matter the channel, you knew you were getting the Sears AC commercial at some point during Gilligan's Island.

What a time to be alive. What a country.

OK, let's jump back to 2026 (sadly) and get this class started with Brittany Mahomes hitting the gym and reminding America she's still very much in her prime:

"Archives never expire," Mahomes captioned the above post. No idea what that means, but who am I to question it? I haven't been to a gym in a decade.

Welcome back to class, Brittany! Been a while. Some folks tend to forget about Brittany Mahomes in Kansas City with Taylor Swift now a permanent resident, but I'd tread lightly with that one.

She's still very much the First Lady of Arrowhead. Don't get it twisted. The Chiefs still haven't lost a game this season, and I don't expect that to change this weekend against the Chargers.

Patrick's locked in, and so is Brittany Mahomes. Good luck, NFL.

Now, speaking of the AFC West ...

Let's go ahead and check in with Ryan Fitzpatrick after Denver's huge OT win last night. Surely morale is HIGH right now ...

Right?

"Bo Nix is not playing competitively. It’s almost disrespectful to the quarterback position how he’s playing football right now."

My goodness. What an absolute butt-chewing from Ryan Fitzpatrick here. I've never seen an analyst just obliterate a player like that ... after a win!

Some folks are jumping all over Fitzy today, by the way. I think that's ridiculous. He's 100000% right in everything he said. Everything.

Bo Nix was atrocious last night. Denver was beyond anemic on offense. Nix finished with 107 yards on 17 completions, and barely — and I mean barely — threw the ball beyond the line of scrimmage.

In fact, according to CBS researcher Doug Clawson, he currently ranks 701st out of 701 qualified quarterbacks over the last two decades (!!!) in average pass length (4.9 air yards per attempt).

That's indescribably bad. It's unfathomable. I watched Tua Tagovailoa dink and dunk for years in Miami. Bo Nix last night made Tua look like Dan Marino!

And everyone's jumping on Fitzpatrick for ... being mean? Give me a break.

Grow up.

OK, let's rapid-fire this Friday class into a big weekend of FOOTBALL! First up? For those who missed it, college football is closing in on a 24-team playoff starting next season.

Twenty-four.

I don't know about you, but it makes me sad:

So, we're going to lose conference championship games, which is a huge bummer. They obviously still don't mean quite as much as they used to, but that first Saturday in December is always one of the best Saturdays of the year. It's gone now.

That's obviously a con.

As for the a pro? Well, we do get a ton of actual playoff games on campuses. That's a no-brainer. My biggest issue with the current format is the lack of on-campus games. It's silly. Most of these games should be on campus. It's what makes college football so great.

Do I think this will kill college football like a lot of folks are forecasting today? No. Do I think "November games are going to be totally useless" like a lot of folks are forecasting today? No. There will still be important games in November.

But ...

The regular season as a whole will absolutely lose some juice. Can't really argue that. The college football regular season used to be the best regular season in all of sports because the margin for error was so thin. It's why Tim Tebow famously cried after losing to Ole Miss back in 2008.

That's gone now. Losing 2, 3, or even 4 games in some cases won't kill you anymore. That's a bummer. A big one.

I'm quite sure you all have opinions on this. Believe me, I see the OutKick newsletter email account. It's loaded today.

So ... let me know what you think! Zach.Dean@OutKick.com. (Gulp).

OK, that's it for today — and this week! Good work, everyone. On the way out, let's go from football to futbol and end our week with the greatest penalty kick you've ever seen.

Have a big October weekend, everyone.

item.title: Trump hosted a dinner with – wait for it – Stephen A Smith, Kid Rock and Bill Maher
item.description: Trump hosted Kid Rock, Bill Maher, and Stephen A. Smith for a dinner that Kid Rock called "epic" during his "Fox & Friends" appearance Friday.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump hosted a dinner on Thursday night with, wait for it, singer Kid Rock, HBO host Bill Maher and ESPN commentator Stephen A. Smith.

Kid Rock, whose real name is Robert Ritchie, mentioned the dinner during a Friday morning appearance on Fox News’ "Fox & Friends," calling the gathering "epic."

The singer said the four men agreed on at least one point: "Socialism and communism have no place to have a foothold in our government."

It's not entirely clear why Trump assembled that particular group for dinner. However, Rock said he and Maher recently joined Trump for a separate meal that also included UFC president Dana White.

Apparently, Smith served as the sports representative this time.

BILL MAHER REVEALS HE'S HAVING DINNER WITH TRUMP AGAIN, SAYS HE WAS 'REALLY NICE' BY TEXT

To the group's credit, there was at least some political diversity at the table. Kid Rock is an avid Trump supporter. Maher is a liberal who has become increasingly critical of both parties and the progressive left. Smith is, well, politically inconsistent.

We suspect Smith played the role of proud moderate Thursday night, as he often does when appearing on conservative radio and television.

That version of Smith can sound quite different from the one who appears on SiriusXM and his YouTube channel, where he is far more sensitive to the concerns of liberals and what he frequently calls the Black community.

Smith says he will address the dinner Friday night on his podcast.

Our prediction: He will downplay the chummy nature of the gathering, stress that attending dinner with Trump does not mean he supports him, and claim he pushed the president on racial issues. He will then offer a somewhat different account the next time a conservative interviews him.

Maher, meanwhile, is probably the most likely member of the group to provide a straightforward account of what actually happened. We do not doubt the evening was as entertaining as Kid Rock suggests.

Still, the dinner is notable for another reason. Trump remains one of the few major politicians in 2026 who regularly sits down with people who openly disagree with him. Few political commentators have been more consistently critical of Trump than Maher, including after the two first had dinner together last year.

In any event, a dinner with Trump, Kid Rock, Maher, and Smith could be good fodder for Saturday Night Live this weekend.

So long as they don't mention anything about women at the gym, of course

item.title: Selma Blair's rep speaks out after star's arrest: 'Much more to this story'
item.description: Selma Blair's rep says the actress had a medical emergency on the Delta flight and that authorities took her service dog, adding that she did not intend any harm.
item.content:encoded:
Selma Blair is speaking out for the first time since her arrest.

On Friday, Blair's representative issued a lengthy statement to People, saying the actress "did not intend to harm anyone."

"Since Sunday night, the public account of what happened to Selma aboard a flight to New York has been built almost entirely on a police statement and a decade-old headline," the spokesperson said.

"A handful of journalists have taken the time to report on Selma as a human being rather than a headline, and we are grateful to them," the statement continued. "But fair reporting has been the exception, and in the space left by our silence, speculation has hardened into something being treated as fact. We can, however, correct the record on a few points already in public circulation. Selma Blair experienced a medical emergency on the flight. There was no attempt to open the door of the aircraft. Selma did not intend to harm anyone."

SELMA BLAIR ARRESTED AFTER IN-FLIGHT INCIDENT

In 2018, Blair revealed publicly that she was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, an autoimmune disease.

"The suggestion by anyone that Selma does not have multiple sclerosis is outrageous. Her diagnosis has been public since 2018. What Selma has been able to do physically in the years since is nothing short of a miracle. She still has bad days, and she lives with pain daily," the statement continued. "Selma also has pseudobulbar affect, a neurological condition secondary to her MS, which bears directly on how a medical episode presents to people who do not know her. For the same reason, she travels with a service dog who doesn’t leave her side, and the authorities took her dog from her."

Blair's rep went on to share the list of projects the star has been involved in this year.

SELMA BLAIR'S LAWYER CITES MISSED MEDICATION, HEAD INJURY AFTER IN-FLIGHT ARREST: WHAT DOCTORS SAY

"[Blair] has worked on seven film and television projects in 2026 alone, only a couple of which have been announced. She has launched a skin care line, a clothing line, and a line of eye-glass readers, each built around the idea of beauty and utility for people whose bodies do not always cooperate. She remains a visible and relentless advocate for disability rights, for the MS community, and this year for the Jewish community in the face of rising antisemitism, including from the stage of the ADL’s State of the Arts event at The Jewish Museum two weeks ago. Selma had never been arrested before Sunday night," the statement said.

It concluded, "There is much more to this story than has been reported, and we ask to consider the entirety of the facts before rushing to judgment, whether in the courtroom or in the court of public opinion."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Blair was arraigned Monday on two counts of second-degree assault stemming from accusations that she assaulted a nurse and a police officer after an incident involving crew members aboard a Delta Air Lines flight to New York City. Blair pleaded not guilty. 

The judge set bail at $20,000 cash/$60,000 bond/ $60,000 partially secured bond. She's expected in court in January 2027.

The actress was arrested Sunday.

"On Sunday October 11 at approximately 11pm at JFK Airport, PAPD responded to a call about a physically abusive passenger aboard Delta Airlines flight 938 which was parked at the gate after arrival from LAX," New York Port Authority officials confirmed to Fox News Digital.

"Suspect was identified as Selma Blair, a 54-year-old woman. She was taken into custody and transported to the hospital for evaluation."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

During her court appearance in Queens, Blair’s lawyer claimed the actress missed multiple doses of a "powerful" medication, the New York Post reported.

WATCH: Selma Blair exits Queens Criminal Court

"This was not an intentional assault," the outlet noted that her attorney, Shawn Barnes, said in court. "Ms. Blair missed several doses of… a powerful medication that controls severe neurological symptoms."

"Ms. Blair boarded this flight after being on set and working extensive hours and exhaustive hours in the days leading up to this flight," he added. "Additionally, at one point, during the flight, there was an incident where Miss Blair actually fell and hit her head," Barnes added, according to the NY Post. "These factors, coupled with altitude, resulted in a state of severe confusion and disorientation."

Blair was restrained on a stretcher at the airport but freed her leg, and allegedly kicked an officer in the face, neck and chest, causing substantial swelling, court documents said.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

A nurse at Jamaica Hospital Medical Center, where Blair was taken, alleged that the actress kicked her in the chest while moving her.

Delta confirmed that law enforcement officials responded to an incident upon arrival to John F. Kennedy International Airport, a flight which departed out of Los Angeles earlier in the day.

"Delta has zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behavior, as the safety of our customers and crew always comes first," Delta said in a statement.

Additionally, there was no operational impact on the flight as it landed ahead of schedule at JFK, Delta said.

Sources told TMZ that Blair allegedly punched one flight attendant and bit another in the middle of the flight.

Law enforcement officials confirmed Blair was also separately served with a summons by the FBI, and is currently facing one charge of assault.

item.title: Joe Rogan defends Shane Gillis from 'word police' after SNL joke sparks liberal uproar

COMEDIAN TIM DILLON SLAMS SYDNEY SWEENEY CRITICS UPSET WITH STEAMY AD: 'HOW INSANE IS THAT? '

item.content:encoded:
A Philly gay sports bar will close its doors this weekend after members of the LGBTQIA+ community accused it of a cocktail of egregious behavior, including transphobia, misogyny and a slew of microaggressions.

With Game 1 of the WNBA Finals set for Saturday afternoon, instead of a celebration of everything queer, Marsha's South Street will hold its own funeral. After facing serious allegations of the bar not being gay enough, Black queer bar owner Chivonn Anderson tried to hold on for dear life, but ultimately she was left no choice but to call it quits during the Holy Grail for gay sports bars.

"It is with heavy hearts that we have decided to close Marsha’s doors for good. We have loved serving this community, and still believe that more than ever this city needs more women/queer/BIPOC- owned businesses," Anderson wrote Thursday on the bar's Instagram page.

"For all of our beloved regulars and supporters- we will miss you! Please come by this weekend and say goodbye. We will be open Friday, Saturday, and Sunday for one last hurrah before we shut down," she added.

How is it possible for a Philly gay sports bar not to be gay enough? This all started back in April when Black trans manager and bartender Olivia Rhodes claimed that the place was a hellhole for gays to work. "Marsha’s may claim to be a queer safe space, but it is nothing like that," Rhodes said on Instagram.

It was the ultimate insult.

Word quickly got around. Fair or not, Marsha's was in trouble. Rhodes also claimed the bar's general manager, Rylan, said that nonbinary queers were "overly emotional, too sensitive" and that the place needed to hire more men because the bar could use "more testosterone."

You get the point. The workers wanted this place to be way gayer. More trans.

"Marsha's has a long history of misogyny, and racism that doesn't align with the queer identity it claims and represents," Rhodes charged.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Another former worker, who is a biracial, bisexual woman, claimed she was treated poorly, too. There were also allegations levied on Reddit by an employee who says the head chef misgendered workers. "Marsha's is actively and explicitly not a queer space, it's at BEST a space for cis white lesbians to come ogle the 3-4 minorities that come through on any given night and at worst it's just a straight sports bar half-heartedly marketed as vaguely lesbian adjacent," a Reddit user added.

Anderson tried her best to weather the storm. She even bent the knee in a September Instagram post that was clearly a full-court shot to save her business as the WNBA playoffs were firing on all cylinders.

"We have trained staff on biased language and microaggressions," the bar owner wrote. "We enforce a zero-tolerance policy against hate and bias. We have worked with, and will continue to work with, amazing restorative justice practitioners in our community that have held us accountable. We have done the work, and we want to keep growing."

Too late. The gays already canceled you, Chivonn. Now you're hosting a funeral as Angel Reese tips off her first WNBA Finals.

Mission accomplished.

item.title: Biden judge rejects Obama CIA chief's legal bid against Trump over one key problem
item.description: John Brennan's lawsuit against Trump and senior officials was dismissed, but grand jury investigations into the former CIA director continue.
item.content:encoded:
A Biden-appointed judge dismissed former CIA Director John Brennan's lawsuit against President Donald Trump and senior administration officials, ruling that his concerns about the potential destruction of evidence needed for a future criminal defense were too "speculative."

The dismissal comes as Brennan faces two federal investigations, including a Justice Department probe into whether former intelligence officials conspired to violate Trump's civil rights through investigations into alleged ties between his 2016 presidential campaign and Russia. 

A separate investigation is examining whether Brennan made false statements during 2023 congressional testimony about the Steele dossier's role in a 2017 intelligence assessment of Russian interference in the presidential election.

FORMER CIA DIRECTOR BRENNAN SUBPOENAED TO TESTIFY IN FEDERAL TRUMP CONSPIRACY CASE

Trump has repeatedly accused Brennan, President Barack Obama and other former intelligence officials of orchestrating the "Russia collusion hoax," but they have rejected those accusations, claiming that the administration is attempting to discredit legitimate intelligence findings about Russian interference in the 2016 election.

While Judge Jia Cobb called Brennan’s allegations that the Trump administration was targeting him for opposing the president "deeply concerning," she ruled that he lacked standing to sue because he had not shown that officials were likely destroying records relevant to a potential defense, and the injury he feared depended on a series of events that had not yet occurred.

"For Brennan’s constitutional injury to actually accrue, a series of dominoes must fall, and Defendants’ deletion of records is just one of those dominoes," Cobb wrote. 

"There is no dispute about this: Defendants describe this domino chain in their motion to dismiss ... and Brennan accepts it in his response."

Brennan has been identified as a target in two federal investigations that have involved three grand jury inquiries — two in the Southern District of Florida and one in Washington, D.C. — but he has not been charged with a crime. The former CIA director was subpoenaed to testify before a federal grand jury in Fort Pierce, Florida, Oct. 15, though his scheduled appearance was postponed.

Brennan filed his lawsuit naming Trump, FBI Director Kash Patel, Attorney General Todd Blanche, CIA Director John Ratcliffe and other officials July 1, 2026. The 46-page lawsuit accused the Justice Department of handling its investigation into Brennan with "unprecedented, irregular conduct" that was driven by the "president’s retribution agenda."

DELETED EMAIL DETAILS ALLEGED TRUMP-TARGETING PUSH INSIDE LETITIA JAMES’ OFFICE: ‘FIND AND PURSUE CRIMES’

Brennan argued that key evidence could disappear before he had a chance to challenge any future indictment. He pointed to deleted social media posts, the administration’s use of Signal and other messaging tools with auto-delete features, unpreserved texts and direct messages, AI queries, Microsoft Teams chats and alleged failures to preserve discovery in other cases, including the prosecution of Rep. LaMonica McIver, D-N.J. 

He said the loss of those records could make it harder to determine whether the investigations were based on legitimate law enforcement concerns or political retaliation.

"With this lawsuit, Director Brennan has served notice that the government’s conduct and its document preservation will be carefully scrutinized in the event of any future indictment," Brennan’s lawyers, Ken Wainstein and Dan Gelber, told the AP.

"Director Brennan will continue to vigorously defend himself against these baseless investigations, and he will challenge any attempt to use the criminal justice system for personal and political retribution." 

The lawsuit also pointed to what it described as irregularities in the Justice Department’s handling of the investigation.

It cited the removal of longtime DOJ prosecutor Maria Medetis Long, who was reportedly taken off the Brennan investigation in April 2026 after expressing doubts about the strength of the case, as evidence of what it described as irregular conduct. She was replaced by Trump ally Joseph diGenova, who later resigned from his role overseeing the investigation amid reported internal disagreements over the handling of the case.

TRUMP SAYS HE WILL NOMINATE ACTING AG TODD BLANCHE TO PERMANENTLY LEAD JUSTICE DEPARTMENT

Brennan’s attorneys accused the Justice Department of "judge-shopping" by trying to steer grand jury proceedings toward Trump-appointed Judge Aileen Cannon in Fort Pierce, Florida, rather than allowing the case to proceed through the court's normal assignment process. They also questioned why prosecutors were pursuing the investigation in Florida when much of the allegations occurred in Washington, D.C.

The complaint also accused DOJ and FBI leaders of improperly discussing details of the investigations publicly, raising questions about whether officials disclosed information that should have remained confidential.

It cited Attorney General Todd Blanche’s statements that DOJ had issued "200 grand jury subpoenas" and was investigating a "pattern of behavior" to "destroy" Trump, as well as FBI Director Kash Patel’s public discussion of the investigations and their targets.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Justice Department for comment.

item.content:encoded:
Bryan Kohberger's new lawyer is taking another swing at Idaho prosecutors in his fight to have the judge who called his client a "faceless coward" removed from post-conviction proceedings.

Court-appointed attorney Greg Rauch is accusing Latah County prosecutors of "regurgitating" rules rather than addressing concerns raised in his motion to disqualify Judge Steven Hippler from the case.

Hippler said Kohberger, 31, "slithered" into the victims' home before committing a crime that made him "the worst of the worst" after the killer admitted guilt last year.

At issue, according to Rauch, "is how [Hippler's] statements about counsel’s preparation and [Kohberger's] capacity for truthfulness bear on the disputes it may now decide, in combination with the myriad of other statements made."

KOHBERGER PROSECUTORS SAY NO AS IDAHO KILLER TRIES TO BOOT JUDGE WHO CALLED HIM A 'FACELESS COWARD'

"Even if I could force him to speak, which legally I cannot, how could anyone ever be assured that what he speaks is the truth?" Hippler asked during sentencing. "Do we really believe, after all of this, he is capable of speaking the truth, or of giving up something of himself to help the very people whose lives he destroyed? Rather, I suspect the so-called reason would be dished out in enticing self-serving and aggrandizing untruthful bits, leaving people wanting more information, more insight, and thus enhancing even further the power he seeks to hold."

BRYAN KOHBERGER DIDN'T UNDERSTAND WHAT HE WAS DOING WHEN HE PLEADED GUILTY: UNSEALED MEMO

"This motion does not rest upon one adverse ruling, one harsh statement, or the mere fact that the judge who presided over Bryan Kohberger’s criminal case has been assigned to his post-conviction proceeding," Rauch wrote in his initial 22-page motion on Aug. 27. "It rests upon the extraordinary convergence of all of them."

Hippler had rejected a request for more time for Kohberger's previous defense lawyer, Anne Taylor, and in a June 26 order, described her complaints about discovery as "ultimately empty" while suggesting she was simply trying to delay his trial.

Prosecutors, in an opposition to the motion filed earlier this month, wrote that Kohberger had failed to show Hippler "is biased."

item.title: Major US grocery chains hit by cybersecurity incident
item.description: Ahold Delhaize's cybersecurity incident knocked online ordering and digital coupons offline at Stop & Shop, Food Lion, Hannaford and Giant Food stores.
item.content:encoded:
You pull out your phone to check your grocery store's digital coupons or place an order for dinner. Suddenly, the app won't open. The website is unavailable, and the groceries you were counting on for tonight may never arrive. For anyone who depends on online grocery shopping, that's a frustrating problem.

That's the situation shoppers encountered this week at several major U.S. supermarket chains. A cybersecurity incident at grocery giant Ahold Delhaize forced the company to take some systems offline. The disruption affected Stop & Shop, Food Lion, Hannaford and the Giant supermarket chains. The company says its physical stores have remained open, although customers have experienced interruptions to online services.

There's another reason this story deserves attention. The same company suffered a major data breach in 2024 that exposed personal information belonging to more than 2.2 million people. So, as investigators work to understand the latest incident, shoppers have a reasonable question: Could their personal information be at risk again?

CHICK-FIL-A DATA BREACH EXPOSES CUSTOMER ACCOUNTS

Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money

In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will share five practical ways to protect your trip and your wallet this holiday travel season. You’ll learn how to secure your phone and personal information, find better travel deals, avoid common scams, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Join us Saturday, October 31, at 11 AM ET / 8 AM PT. Register free now at CyberGuyLive.com.

FRENCH SUPERMARKETS FACE MILLIONS IN LOSSES AFTER CYBERATTACK HITS REFRIGERATORS NATIONWIDE

On Oct. 12, Ahold Delhaize confirmed a cybersecurity issue within its network. The Netherlands-based company owns some of America's best-known regional supermarket chains and operates more than 9,400 stores worldwide. The company took certain systems offline to protect its operations while security teams investigated the problem. In its official statement, Ahold Delhaize said: "Our teams are taking steps to assess and mitigate the issue. This includes taking some systems offline to help protect them."

The company serves approximately 60 million customers each week across its international businesses. Consequently, a problem involving its technology can affect grocery shopping far beyond a single store.

The cybersecurity incident has disrupted online services for five major U.S. supermarket chains:

According to Grocery Dive, websites and mobile apps for all five chains were still unavailable on the morning of Wednesday, Oct. 14. That marked at least the third consecutive day of online disruptions. Customers have encountered problems accessing online ordering and digital coupons. Some app-based loyalty features have also been unavailable. In its Oct. 13 update, Ahold Delhaize said it was beginning a controlled relaunch of certain systems. However, as of Oct. 14, the company had not announced a firm timetable for restoring all affected services.

Yes. In its Oct. 13 statement, Ahold Delhaize confirmed that its supermarkets across Europe and the United States remained open and were serving customers. Notices from the affected U.S. chains also indicated that pharmacies were operating during their normal business hours. However, online shopping has experienced significant disruptions. Customers have faced interruptions to grocery pickup and delivery services. Meanwhile, shoppers who rely on digital coupons have encountered problems accessing their usual discounts.

As of Oct. 14, Food Lion, Giant Food and The Giant Company also directed customers to third-party delivery services, including Instacart, DoorDash and Uber Eats, where available. For customers who depend on grocery delivery because of mobility challenges or limited transportation, these disruptions can create a serious inconvenience.

If you placed an online grocery order that was never fulfilled, the affected supermarket chains said customers would receive refunds for those orders. However, it's worth checking your credit card or bank account to make sure the refund actually arrives.

Keep your original order confirmation and any emails related to the purchase. If the refund doesn't appear within the retailer's stated processing period, contact customer service through a verified channel. If your grocery app remains unavailable, shopping inside a physical store may be your most dependable option. Still, consider calling ahead if you need a specific service or want to confirm that a prescription is ready.

On Oct. 13, Ahold Delhaize issued a statement, updated Oct. 14, saying it was in the process of starting a controlled relaunch of certain systems. The company said it was working with external cybersecurity experts and appropriate authorities to investigate the incident. In a direct response to CyberGuy, an Ahold Delhaize USA spokesperson provided an update on efforts to restore affected services. "Please know our teams are working as quickly as possible to restore systems safely that we took offline as a precautionary measure, including our websites," the spokesperson told CyberGuy.

The spokesperson also confirmed that stores remain open and apologized for the disruption to customers. However, Ahold Delhaize has not publicly identified who caused the problem or explained how its network was compromised. It has also not confirmed whether ransomware played a role. That leaves several important questions unanswered, including how the incident began and when all affected services will be restored. The company has not provided a firm timetable for full restoration.

This may be the biggest concern for shoppers who have online grocery accounts. In its statement, Ahold Delhaize said investigators had found no evidence at that point that customer, employee or partner data was taken during the incident. That's encouraging for shoppers who have provided personal information to these supermarket chains. However, investigators were still examining the incident as of that update. The company's preliminary findings do not definitively rule out data theft. As of Oct. 14, Ahold Delhaize had not confirmed that personal information was stolen during this latest incident. That means shoppers should remain alert without assuming their personal information has been compromised.

Unfortunately, this isn't the first major cybersecurity incident involving Ahold Delhaize. In November 2024, hackers gained unauthorized access to internal U.S. business systems operated by Ahold Delhaize USA Services. The attackers obtained files containing sensitive personal information. The company eventually disclosed that more than 2.2 million people were affected. According to a filing with the Maine Attorney General, the breach involved approximately 2.24 million individuals. In a June 2025 breach notification, the company explained that the stolen information varied by person.

The vast majority of those affected were current or former employees, along with their dependents and beneficiaries. For many of us, grocery shopping now involves much more than walking into a store with a shopping list. We create accounts, save payment details and use loyalty programs to access discounts. Even without confirmed customer data theft, a widely reported cybersecurity incident can give scammers opportunities to target shoppers. These seven precautions can help you protect your information and avoid additional headaches.

Scammers may send emails or text messages claiming that you need to verify your payment information to receive a grocery refund. Those messages can seem especially convincing if you've recently had an order canceled. Avoid clicking unexpected refund links. Instead, review your original payment account or contact the retailer using a verified phone number. Never provide your banking password or pay a processing fee to receive a refund.

If you placed an order around the time of the outage, check whether the store charged you for groceries you never received. Save your confirmation emails and keep any receipts. Then, review your account for a refund. If the money doesn't appear within the retailer's stated processing period, contact customer service or your payment provider.

If you reuse your grocery account password on other websites, replace it with a unique one. A password manager can generate and store strong passwords without forcing you to remember each one. A real cybersecurity incident gives scammers an opportunity to send convincing fake breach notifications. You might receive a message claiming that your grocery account has been compromised and that you must immediately verify your identity. Before entering personal information, confirm the alert through the retailer's official communications.

Although Ahold Delhaize reported no evidence of data theft in its Oct. 14 update, regularly checking your financial accounts remains a smart precaution. Enable transaction alerts through your bank or credit card provider. Pay attention to unfamiliar charges or unexpected account activity.

If you normally use your grocery store's app to access digital coupons or loyalty rewards, check your receipt carefully. Some discounts may be unavailable while the retailer's online services are down. Before checking out, ask a store employee whether there's another way to receive an advertised discount. Keep your receipt if you believe you were overcharged so you can request an adjustment when customer service becomes available.

If you clicked a suspicious grocery refund or security alert link, your next steps depend on what information you shared. If you entered your password, change it immediately through the retailer's official website once it's available. Update any other accounts using that password. If you provided credit card or banking information, contact your financial institution and ask about securing your account. item.title: ‘Buck’ stops at Walz: Flanagan ducks Minnesota fraud blame as GOP rival exposes glaring contradiction
item.description: Michele Tafoya, the Republican nominee, hammered Democratic Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan over Minnesota's $9 billion fraud scandal during their debate.
item.content:encoded:
Michele Tafoya, the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Minnesota and a former broadcaster, aggressively sought to put her opponent, Democratic Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, on the defensive during a debate Friday afternoon over the billion-dollar fraud schemes that drew national attention to the state earlier this year.

Early in the debate, Tafoya pressed Flanagan on her qualifications for federal office, pointing to her record as lieutenant governor.

"My opponent has been second in command in this state for eight years, drawing a taxpayer-funded paycheck. And what do we have to show for that? We have massive fraud, historic fraud. We have test scores down. We have crime spiking. We have a massive surplus turned into a deficit," Tafoya said.

TAFOYA MAKES 'COMMON SENSE' PITCH TO DISAFFECTED DEMOCRATS AS SHE VOWS TO FIGHT MINNESOTA’S ‘SOCIALIST LURCH’

"This election is about Peggy Flanagan."

Local and federal investigators have uncovered myriad fraud schemes involving daycare centers, food programs, health clinics and other operations accused of defrauding the state of up to $9 billion. Investigators say fraudsters either inflated the number of people they allegedly helped or fabricated their services altogether — all while receiving government dollars.

When the issue resurfaced later in the debate, the moderator asked Flanagan directly whether, in her view, she had "any ownership over the fraud."

Flanagan sought to distance herself from the issue, pointing to Walz's acknowledgment that responsibility for oversight rested with him.

"The governor has been very clear that the buck stops with him," Flanagan said.

"He was the one who had oversight here. I've led on issues like paid family and medical leave, nation-leading child tax credit, making sure that kids get breakfast and lunch at school. Those are the things and those are the areas where I took the lead."

When Flanagan then redirected the conversation to criticism of President Donald Trump, Tafoya went on the attack.

DAVID MARCUS: PEGGY FLANAGAN'S DEI RECORD AND FRAUD SCANDAL PUT MINNESOTA SENATE RACE IN THE SPOTLIGHT

"Peggy, Donald Trump isn't on the ballot. You and I are on the ballot, and only one of us let $9 billion walk out the door to fraud to suggest that we that she somehow is going to be a fraud czar all of a sudden," Tafoya said.

"My goodness, she was second in charge in this state, and she's just going to point her finger at Gov. Tim Walz when she demanded to be in the room where everything happened. But, suddenly, she has nothing to do with this. Again, sell it to someone else," she added.

Flanagan has served as Minnesota's lieutenant governor for nearly eight years, taking office in 2019. By the time Walz announced that he would not run for re-election as governor amid political scrutiny for the fraud, Flanagan had already announced her bid for U.S. Senate.

Responding to Tafoya, Flanagan doubled down on her criticism of Trump, noting that the president had recently endorsed Tafoya.

"Donald Trump doesn't just endorse anybody. In fact, he endorses against people in his own party if they dare to take him on. Michele Tafoya passed his litmus test with flying colors," Flanagan said.

Tafoya then laid out her own proposals for combating fraud, including tougher consequences for noncitizens who defraud Americans.

"No. 1, if you're a guest of this country, and you defraud Americans, you must leave. You must leave, and you should have no pathway back," she said.

FRAUD EXPERT EXPOSES HOW HIDDEN NETWORKS DROVE MINNESOTA FRAUD, OTHER MAJOR SCAMS: 'CRIMINAL ENTERPRISE'

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"No. 2, if you're an American and you defraud your fellow Americans, we should be talking about mandatory prison minimums. Tough sentences, not an easygoing slap on the wrist. 

"And No. 3, if you're a state like Minnesota who cannot keep your financial house in order, why would the federal government release billions and billions of dollars to you, only to see it go to fraud?"

After securing their respective parties’ nominations earlier this year, Flanagan and Tafoya will face off in the state’s Nov. 3 general election.

item.title: Former University of Kentucky cheerleader sentenced to 10 years in prison for infant's death

item.content:encoded:
Laken Snelling, a former University of Kentucky cheerleader, was sentenced to 10 years in prison Friday, according to local media, after being convicted of first-degree manslaughter for the death of her infant child.

Snelling, who was indicted for manslaughter and three other charges in March, pleaded guilty in August.

Officers from the Lexington Police Department arrested Snelling in August 2025 after her roommates heard loud noises coming from her closet. When officers arrived on scene, they found the infant cold to the touch and wrapped in a trash bag placed in the closet, the city of Lexington announced in a statement.

ARIZONA WOMAN CHARGED WITH KILLING NEWBORN CHILD 45 YEARS AFTER BODY WAS FOUND

The infant was born alive and died from asphyxiation, the Kentucky Medical Examiner's Office determined, according to the Lexington statement. When Judge Diane Minnifield asked Snelling how she ended the infant's life, she replied, "I deprived him of oxygen."

"I was under a lot of emotional stress and my baby came unexpectedly," Snelling said through tears while in court. "And instead of helping him, I ended his life and afterward I cleaned up and didn’t tell anyone."

IDAHO MOM WHO CLAIMED VACCINES KILLED HER TWIN BABIES CHARGED WITH MURDERING HER KIDS

In addition to the manslaughter charge, Snelling pleaded guilty to charges of abuse of a corpse, tampering with physical evidence and concealing the birth of an infant.

Snelling, who was a senior at the time, told investigators that she was awake for 30 minutes after giving birth, but then passed out on top of the baby.

When she woke up, she saw the infant "turning blue and purple," according to court documents.

NEW HAMPSHIRE SUPREME COURT OVERTURNS ADAM MONTGOMERY'S MURDER CONVICTION IN DAUGHTER HARMONY'S DEATH

Investigators also found that Snelling had deleted photos of her labor from her phone and other evidence of her pregnancy, according to court documents.

item.title: Lawyers for girl alleging sexual assault by trans wrestler fire back at Washington officials in SCOTUS appeal
item.description: A Washington high school wrestler asks the Supreme Court for protection before wrestling season, alleging sexual assault by a transgender opponent.
item.content:encoded:
A Washington high school wrestler who alleges she was sexually assaulted by a transgender opponent during a girls’ match is asking the Supreme Court to intervene before her next season begins, and her attorneys are firing back after the defendants tried to write off her claimed harm as "manufactured."

In an Oct. 15 filing, her attorneys at Alliance Defending Freedom accused the three defendants, the Puyallup School District, Washington’s Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction and the Washington Interscholastic Activities Association, of shifting responsibility for providing those protections.

"Defendants’ briefs mostly point the finger at each other, trying to pass the buck for the harm inflicted," Alliance Defending Freedom (ADF) attorneys wrote in an Oct. 15 reply supporting the girl, Kallie Keeler and her mother, Stephanie Brown.

WOMEN WHO FACED BIOLOGICAL MALES IN GIRLS' SPORTS AND LOCKER ROOMS SPEAK OUT AHEAD OF WASHINGTON STATE VOTE

"Exit isn’t accommodation. It’s the injury, and Brown and K.M.K. are suffering it now," the attorneys added, rejecting the argument that withdrawing from competition adequately addresses the family’s concerns.

Keeler, identified in court as K.M.K., alleges a transgender opponent sexually assaulted her during a girls’ wrestling match in December 2025. Pierce County prosecutors declined to file criminal charges. Her family is seeking protection against being matched with male opponents while its lawsuit proceeds.

The reply follows opposition briefs from the Puyallup School District, Washington’s Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction and the Washington Interscholastic Activities Association.

"The ‘irreparable’ nature of Applicants’ claimed harm is manufactured," the state argued, challenging the asserted emergency and likelihood of future injury. The statement addressed the justification for immediate court intervention, rather than characterizing the alleged assault as fabricated.

The district said Brown could decline matches without district-imposed penalties. It also cited supportive measures, an expedited school transfer and an ongoing independent Title IX investigation. The defendants raised concerns about their authority to control matchups, competition rules and other students’ privacy.

ADF countered that the defendants collectively control eligibility, participation and competition rules.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

"Defendants each disclaim full power, but in so doing, they ignore that together they hold it all," the reply states.

The attorneys also challenged the suggestion that the family should await the ordinary appeals process. The district’s appellate answering brief is due Nov. 19, three days after wrestling practices begin, according to its opposition and WIAA’s calendar. ADF said the extension was granted over the family’s objection.

Alongside its Title IX request, ADF outlined an alternative accommodation based on parental rights: Officials would withdraw Keeler, or notify her mother so she could withdraw her, when they know or have reason to know an opponent is male.

Under that proposal, Keeler would receive treatment comparable to the most favorably treated forfeiture allowed by the rules, such as a medical forfeiture. In a tournament, her opponent could advance while she continued in the applicable consolation bracket.

"Her opponent advances, and she stays in the tournament," ADF wrote.

The district court and Ninth Circuit previously denied temporary relief. The Supreme Court application remained pending Friday, with the docket listing the family’s reply but no ruling.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV seen for first time since lung cancer surgery amid major recovery milestone
item.description: The Vatican released first photos of Pope Leo XIV celebrating mass at Gemelli Hospital, days after surgeons removed a lung lobe due to adenocarcinoma.
item.content:encoded:
Pope Leo XIV is up and moving after having part of his lung removed.

After undergoing thoracic surgery Tuesday, during which surgeons removed the lower lobe of the pope’s right lung, examination of the tissue confirmed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, or lung cancer, according to the Vatican.

The pope, 71, has spent four days recovering at Gemelli Hospital in Rome, Italy, after the successful procedure.

DR MARC SIEGEL: POPE LEO'S LUNG SURGERY PUTS MODERN MEDICINE ALONGSIDE FAITH

On Friday, the Vatican released the first photos of Pope Leo after the operation.

The pope is pictured standing at an altar in green vestments, celebrating Mass in a makeshift chapel at the hospital where he distributed communion.

According to a Holy See Press Office statement, several members of Gemelli’s medical and nursing staff and members of the Vatican City State Gendarmerie Corps attended the service.

POPE LEO'S LUNG TUMOR RAISES QUESTIONS ABOUT CANCER RISK FOR NONSMOKERS

"In his homily, the pope thanked all the staff — doctors, nurses and orderlies — for the work they do every day caring for patients in their frailty and especially for what they have done and continue to do for him," the statement said.

The Vatican also confirmed on Friday that the pope’s recovery continues with "steady improvement in his overall condition."

Dr. Luigi Carbone and professor Stefano Margaritora added that the pope’s "post-operative recovery allows him to carry out normal daily activities entirely independently."

Pope Leo plans to make his first public appearance since the procedure on Sunday during the noon Angelus, which he normally leads.

NEVER SMOKED A CIGARETTE? YOU COULD STILL BE AT HIGHER RISK FOR LUNG CANCER

Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel said the pope’s procedure included a small incision with VAT (video-assisted thoracoscopy), which involves less pain and has a quicker recovery.

The pope has been in good health "to begin with" and is highly active, which plays a "major role in recovery," Siegel told Fox News Digital.

"Since he wasn’t a smoker and likely had very good underlying lung function, loss of a lobe, when there are three total on the right, shouldn’t have a major impact on daily activity, especially with pain controlled," the doctor added.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

In a separate Fox News Digital interview, Lary Robinson, an oncologist at Moffitt Cancer Center in Tampa, Florida, shared his surprise regarding the pope’s health status.

About 80% of lung cancers occur in people who smoke or have smoked, said Robinson, who has not treated the pope. However, he noted that lung cancer also occurs among never-smokers, including an estimated 10% of male patients and 25% of female patients.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"But [the pope] had surgery and had a lobectomy, so this is usually only done with people who have localized disease, and presumably he had localized disease. And hopefully that's a Stage 1 cancer," the doctor added.

If the pope’s cancer is Stage 1, there is a "high chance" of cure — about 90% — depending on the size of the tumor, the oncologist said. The fact that he went straight to surgery suggests there was likely no evidence that the cancer had spread.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"We'll have to wait for the pathology to determine … whether he needs any additional treatment afterward," Robinson said.

The pope’s anticipated trip to South America in November is reportedly still on schedule, though his participation remains in question based on recovery.
